headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading error: A can process untrusted content while B is explicitly about prompt leaks, creating a plausible instruction-hijack path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A reads/writes files, runs shell/subprocesses, and exposes API surfaces that can ingest content; Agent B is a prompt-leak repository, so its outputs may contain attacker-controlled instructions. With no provenance or isolation documented between them, B’s content could be fed into A and hijack tool use. Uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF B’s leaked prompt text is copied into A’s file or stdin/stdout inputs
IF A parses B-originated content as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Keep B outputs out of A’s prompt and file inputs
Add a provenance tag to any B-derived text before A sees it
Review A prompts for instruction-following on untrusted content
Run A and B in separate workspaces
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches configuration secrets and academic papers, while B has network egress none and no data classes or IO surfaces documented. The pairwise leakage path is therefore limited: B does not appear able to exfiltrate data, and no shared workspace is documented. This is a low-risk, mostly one-way exposure concern.
conditions: IF A’s secrets or papers are copied into B’s prompt context
IF B is extended with any outbound channel not shown in its profile
mitigations: Do not pass A secrets into B prompts
Verify B remains network-disabled
Use separate local workspaces
Redact sensitive fields before any handoff
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on cross-agent transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; B has no write, network, or concurrency surfaces documented. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource access, so direct capability conflict is not established. Because shared state is not stated, uncertainty remains but the blast radius appears small.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF B is given write or API privileges not present in its profile
mitigations: Assign separate directories
Keep B read-only
Avoid concurrent writes from A
Check for hidden shared mounts
requires-engineering: add file-locking or workspace isolation

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing agent with agentic RAG and API endpoints, while B’s repository is about prompt leaks, so B may consume or relay A’s generated text without verification. That creates a plausible chain where A’s outputs become authoritative inputs for B, causing propagated errors or unsafe instructions in default workflows. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF B ingests A-generated text as source material
IF downstream users treat B’s output as authoritative without review
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B
Mark A outputs as untrusted drafts
Require citation checks before reuse
Limit B to summarization, not action-taking
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A handles configuration secrets and academic data, while B is a source-available prompt-leak project with no residency or retention controls documented. If A’s sensitive data is routed into B, compliance gaps around retention and subject handling become plausible. Because only A documents sensitive classes, B is cited for missing controls rather than data handling.
conditions: IF regulated or secret data from A is transferred into B
IF B is deployed in an environment requiring documented retention or residency controls
mitigations: Do not route secrets into B
Document retention for any shared artifacts
Keep regulated data in A only
Review residency requirements before deployment
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
